findings.title: Noul does not say what yes and no mean
findings.message: The question carries no criteria, so where the line between yes and no falls is left to the model.
findings.hint: The instruction is enough for many Nouls. Where the boundary is subtle, saying what a yes and a no mean is what moves a question from guessing to deciding.
findings.suggest: Add a `criteria` object with a `true` and a `false` description, saying which material counts as each.

findings.title: Answering needs arithmetic
findings.message: Answering this needs counting, adding or comparing numbers.
findings.hint: Jev recognises the shape of a count instead of tallying, and the error grows with the size of the thing counted. Comparing a figure with a threshold is not this defect: on decision-v7's policy cases Jev answered 30 of 30 threshold questions correctly. Accept it where the count is small, bounded and visible in one place, such as whether a list has more than one entry, and the answer is a judgement about presence rather than the number itself.
findings.suggest: Do the arithmetic in code. Where the thing being counted is something only a reader can spot, ask one question per candidate and add the answers up yourself.
findings.evidence: Read: "Is the value of 234 × 842 different from 197128?"
